initialContact.message: Hello. I'm 58 and planning to retire at 65. I checked my pension estimate and it will be about €2,100 per month. I currently earn €3,200. I have €45,000 in savings and my mortgage (€180/month) ends in 3 years. Will this be enough? Should I work longer?

problemContext.currentSituation: Planning retirement in 7 years, concerned about income reduction
problemContext.emotionalState: worried, uncertain, wanting to plan properly

idealAdvice: Validate that starting to plan now is smart (7 years is good timeframe)
Calculate actual retirement budget needs (typically 70-80% of current income)
Account for mortgage ending - that frees up €180/month
Explain pension optimization strategies (working a few years longer increases pension significantly)
Review voluntary pension savings options (if wants to boost retirement income)
Consider part-time work in early retirement if desired
Create retirement budget including healthcare, hobbies, travel plans
Discuss inflation protection and investment of savings
commonMistakes: Automatically saying income is too low without analyzing actual needs
Not considering mortgage ending in calculation
Ignoring that expenses typically decrease in retirement
Not asking about desired retirement lifestyle
Pushing aggressive investments without understanding risk tolerance
Not discussing healthcare costs in retirement

initialContact.message: Thank you for the retirement planning help! I made a detailed budget and realized I'll actually be fine with €2,100, especially after the mortgage ends. I'm feeling much better about it. Now I'm thinking about what to do with my €45,000 savings. Should I invest some of it or keep it safe?

problemContext.currentSituation: Retirement anxiety resolved, now optimizing savings strategy

idealAdvice: Acknowledge the great progress in planning
Explain age-based investment strategy (7 years is medium-term horizon)
Suggest balanced portfolio (mix of stocks and bonds appropriate for age)
Keep emergency fund liquid (6 months expenses)
Consider tax-advantaged retirement accounts in Finland
Gradual shift to more conservative investments as retirement approaches
Low-cost index funds or pension insurance products
Review and rebalance annually
commonMistakes: Suggesting high-risk investments too close to retirement
Recommending putting all savings in investments (need emergency fund)

initialContact.message: I've been thinking more about retirement and I'm getting really worried. What if I get sick? What if there's a recession? My friend says I should work until 68 to get maximum pension. Should I give up my retirement plans and work longer? I'm feeling quite stressed about this.

idealAdvice: Address the anxiety with reassurance and facts
Explain Finland's healthcare system coverage in retirement
Discuss emergency fund purpose (handling unexpected costs)
Working longer is an option, not a necessity - depends on health and desires
Break down "what if" scenarios with actual numbers
Each year worked adds about 1.5% to pension in Finland
Create contingency plans rather than worst-case planning
Suggest focusing on what can be controlled
commonMistakes: Automatically agreeing to work longer without discussing quality of life
Not addressing emotional aspects of retirement transition
Providing too many scenarios that increase anxiety
